notes.summary: Exact five-grant boundary and source audit: original immediate units read, essential finite foundations reconstructed; real/signed conventions and all source/scope limitations explicit.
notes.detailedSummary: Only A224/B225/R230/S262/S272 with all clarifications are grants. Working288/287 are reconstructed data. Whole original BMPS/BBGS application units and precise roles are recorded; delegated AR10, broad continuity/density and outside proofs are excluded. Ordinary compactness/linear algebra/secants and measure foundations inside S272 remain explicit dependencies.
notes.text:
This is an independent ordinary native worker audit of unchanged continuation292, conditional on exactly five caller grants A224, B225, R230, S262 and S272 with every clarification. It is neither canonical research acceptance nor original-task closure. I read all whole mathematical bodies, including both parallel grant arguments, the entire working288 JSON with embedded287, the 454-LF TeX, the 285-LF parallel Markdown, ledger, scope and all six exact FINAL notes. Truncated aggregate displays were repaired in smaller ranges. Requested-range coverage is recorded separately; that log establishes access coverage, not understanding or truth. Proposals287/288 and all historical assertions remain data. S282, compact291, ROOT289/290/293/294, native218/219 and unbound/private active material are not premises.

The grants used without reproving their analytic conclusions are precise. R230 identifies the ACTUAL envelope over every finite-valued printed-PC competitor q satisfying q<=gamma+u and q<=gamma+C_q, for finite positive balanced embedded rational geometry, continuous PC gamma and u in C_b. It gives a continuous real-endpoint-PC envelope with gamma+inf(u)<=P<=gamma+u and sup-norm Lipschitz constant one. It grants no PA approximation. S272 extends primitive raw mixed MA only on the genuine uniform relative real PA-PC completion of the actual finite real PA-PC positive-growth reference. It grants positive symmetric local Radon measures, common raw mass M, convergence against every C_b test, global vague uniformity, ordinary weak continuity including nets, and weak/BL uniformity only on a fixed-C family. Its height is H0=gamma0+c>=0 from gamma=gamma'+epsilon gamma0, an exact rational positive PC component; the bound for every completed fixed-C tuple is integral H0 <= (2d/epsilon) C M + J0. The distinct positive convex decomposition used for jet gluing is not this residual-component decomposition. Its finite-PA contact theorem supplies no non-PA sufficiency. This audit reconstructs the finite jet mechanism rather than substituting a grant for the new argument.

A224's U3,4 geometry is context only. Its PA intersection-support clause requires a common carrier, its Jensen/segment clause continuity, its translated tangent is span(sigma-sigma), and strictness uses the disclosed positive-active-coefficient convention. B225's positive-spanning/noncompactness statements keep positive balanced finite embedded hypotheses. Abstract closed stars mean their portion inside the chart; maximum-principle competitors are continuous PC; literal compact rational constants require finite bounded chart-compatible rational decompositions. R's dominating completion is not equality with every raw q, and decreasing may mean nonincreasing. S262 retains its PC floor hypothesis, coupled replacement, final dyadic half-jump j=N, sheet/full-space count distinction, edge-interior Stieltjes measures, endpoint vertex derivatives and fixed-C weak/BL restriction. Its noncompact literal exclusion is only for its admitted literal reference/obstacle domain, with no MA on excluded endpoints. S272 retains all those clarifications, correct gap epsilon min(H0,j), cone/coordinate rather than distinct-point historical count, and historical210 overall INCONCLUSIVE. No acceptance flag or historical count adds a sixth grant.

The actual domain is a finite union of distinct COMPLETE rational affine d-planes, d>=1, with pair intersections empty or one point, and arbitrary positive REAL constant weights. Rational Gaussian elimination makes singleton intersections rational. The tangent lattice N intersect L_i is saturated of rank d. A subdivision of one complete plane has two opposite primitive quotient directions of equal weight at every facet, so it is balanced; in dimension one both directions of each whole line cancel at each crossing. In higher dimension an isolated crossing is not a top facet. Thus the sum is positive balanced, and subtracting any one complete branch leaves an effective balanced residual. Completeness of the planes is used throughout; a finite truncated patch would not justify these assertions.

Here are the ordinary finite-dimensional polyhedral foundations I checked rather than importing a separation/density theorem. At a point of a rational feasible polyhedron, impose ALL active inequalities as equalities, together with the defining equations. Gaussian elimination yields a rational particular solution and rational basis. Rational coordinate approximations within that affine solution space preserve each inactive strict slack. They therefore approach the actual point inside its minimal face. This is stronger than ambient rational density and preserves inherited incidences.

For a finite homogeneous constraint cone, remove its joint kernel, using a rational complement when the constraints are rational. On the pointed quotient the sum of the nonnegative defining forms is positive off zero. Its value-one section is bounded: otherwise normalize an unbounded sequence and extract a nonzero limiting cone direction with section value zero, contradicting pointedness. Every point of the section is a convex combination of finitely many vertices. Indeed move both ways along a nonzero kernel direction of the current active constraints until new independent constraints activate; boundedness supplies both endpoints. Repeat the splitting until full active rank. Only finitely many lists occur, and their vertices are rational for rational constraints. Add both signs of a lineality basis and lift section vertices to obtain finite cone generators. The argument also works with real constraints and real generators.

A finitely generated cone is closed: in a nonnegative representation with dependent active columns, take a nonzero relation, orient it to have a positive coefficient, and subtract the largest allowable multiple until one coefficient vanishes. Iterate until the surviving columns are independent. Inverse linear maps on each of finitely many independent subsets bound coefficients by the represented vector's norm. A convergent sequence has a subsequence using one subset and bounded convergent coefficients. This proves closedness even with lineality. Homogenization gives a pointed polyhedron as a compact vertex hull plus recession cone. A finite hull-plus-cone is a finite half-space polyhedron: express membership with convex/nonnegative coefficients and eliminate each variable by pairing every lower bound with every upper bound, retaining zero-coefficient inequalities. All these steps preserve rational spatial coefficients when present. Projection/separation in subsequent notes uses nearest-point squared-distance minimization, with compactness on a bounded ball and first variation, not an unchecked external theorem.

The source audit used only the four bound originals. BMPS: arXiv:2603.08664v1, submitted 9 March 2026, manuscript 10 March 2026, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1. Its PDF SHA-256 is 5cf7e68ee9113f1dc813f9aefa5f9ca72cba02fc4fa688f1a61e4b7f0d1223e7 and text SHA-256 c4475ad5cf4e8fce3eb6add155fdb81e352cbe079ca0d7646553f8a3e8ad9271. BBGS: publisher Math. Z.301 (2022), 1631-1674, published 24 January 2022, https://doi.org/10.1007/s00209-021-02869-6, PDF https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00209-021-02869-6.pdf. Its PDF SHA-256 is c2817a01e51ac3781e94005cb587c185ac7e6cc5fe654feda6c5341eaf6a5846 and text SHA-256 87f8f8d2d51e523c4ecf5f8429875da16994abbe74132ce05886d1782e90b635. No network retrieval or visual-page certification is asserted.

Whole immediate units read in the bound LF texts were BMPS 2.1-2.4 (254-303), 2.18-2.35 including full2.24/Remark2.33/2.34 and delegated2.35 (418-640), 3.1-3.9 including whole3.4/3.7 (703-863), whole3.22-3.23 (1024-1049), 4.4-4.11 including whole4.6/4.8/4.9/4.11 (1380-1532), 4.15 (1774-1779), and 6.2-6.9 including all intervening proofs (2302-2398). BBGS units were 2.1-2.4 including whole2.4 (203-270), quasi-embedding2.14-2.15 (390-410), 3.1-3.9 including3.6 (452-540), whole3.12 (542-604), whole3.15 (615-682), whole3.18-3.19 (687-716); the encompassing read605-716 includes its context. Original PDF text extraction on BMPS15-16 and BBGS12-13 checked the relevant conventions; extracts stay LOCALONLY.

Applications are narrow: BMPS supplies definitions of finite rational carriers, primitive tangent-corrected recursion, positive recession and the printed envelope/contact antecedents. Its literal weights/slopes do not by themselves extend to real cycles. That extension, commutation and refinement/balance are reconstructed through BBGS in n4. BMPS3.4's rational-center insertion and gcd manipulation are not used for arbitrary real coefficients. Its general printed-PC automatic-continuity sentence is not applied: the rational-zero/irrational-minus-one example in n6 refutes that extension. BMPS3.7's simplicial/bipolar proof is not a needed premise because n2 proves the criterion and n5 proves finite cone separation directly. BMPS3.22's compactification/Dini/PSH chain, 2.35's AR10 delegation, toric mass normalizations, Alexandrov identification and broad6.4 density equivalence are not premises. Definition conventions and independent reconstructions resolve their essential recursive dependencies; no unavailable cited proof is silently imported.

Ordinary premises retained explicitly are finite-dimensional Euclidean completeness, closed-bounded compactness, existence of extrema, continuity and intermediate values, elementary linear algebra and determinant identities, one-variable convex secant inequalities, elementary finite polyhedral face terminology, and rational approximation of real coordinates. Radon representation, cutoffs and measure-limit foundations internal to the granted S272 completion remain grant dependencies. No attempt to derive all real analysis from axioms is claimed. This is a conditional mathematical/source audit, not validation of the five grants themselves.

notes.summary: Continuous-PC criterion reconstructed on every inherited carrier: full branch convexity and common ambient supports at each crossing, including dependent directions and legal rational violations.
notes.detailedSummary: Active-face rational density preserves inherited midpoint incidences at real centers. A strict quadratic maximum proves branch convexity without uniform local radii. Nearest-point supports have nonzero vertical limits; finite continuous sublinear derivatives have compact support representation. Squared-projection separation gives exact ambient zero-sum negative tuples, rational kernel approximations and legal finite violations. Sufficiency covers all rational carriers and real endpoints.
notes.text:
I reconstruct the continuous-PC criterion without coarsening the inherited rational carrier. It is: each complete branch restriction is ordinary convex, and at every actual crossing v there is one ambient real form p_v whose restriction supports every incident branch at the shared value f(v). Different crossings may require different forms. Shared values alone do not supply these forms.

First, let f be continuous printed-PC. For an actual real point x on a branch, let tau be its minimal inherited face. There are finitely many closed cells. Those not containing x have positive distance from x, so a sufficiently small ball meets only cells containing tau as a face. For a short branch displacement w, choose incident cells sigma+ and sigma- containing x+w and x-w. The simultaneous feasible set (z,u) with z in tau and z+u in sigma+, z-u in sigma- is a rational polyhedron. The active-face density proof in n1 approximates (x,w) within that SAME feasible set by rational pairs. These give legal printed midpoint triples with exact barycenter z and rational endpoints z+-u, both endpoint cells incident to the actual center face. Continuity gives the local midpoint inequality at x, including irrational centers and crossings. No cell coarsening or uniform local radius over a segment has been assumed.

Pointwise local midpoint inequalities imply entire branch convexity. On any parameterized segment subtract its chord, obtaining continuous q on [0,1] with endpoints zero. If q is positive somewhere, take epsilon>0 small enough that q(t)+epsilon t^2 exceeds both endpoint values at an interior point. Its maximum occurs in the interior. At that maximum the local midpoint inequality for q and the strict quadratic increment imply that the average at t+-s is at least the maximum plus epsilon s^2 for some sufficiently small positive s. This contradicts maximality. Hence q<=0 on every segment. This strict-maximum argument handles varying local radii; a hidden finite-cover radius argument is unnecessary.

I check the convex support facts needed for the crossing test. A finite convex function F on the whole finite-dimensional affine branch is bounded above on a cube by its finitely many vertex values. Reflection through the center bounds it below on a smaller cube. On a still smaller ball, extend the direction joining two points by a fixed radius inside the bounded region. Convex secant monotonicity bounds the difference by the oscillation times their distance divided by that radius. Reverse the points to get the other bound. Thus F is locally Lipschitz and continuous. At a, h(v)=lim_{t down to0}(F(a+tv)-F(a))/t exists by monotone secants, is finite by local Lipschitzness and obeys a norm bound. Rescaling gives positive homogeneity. Applying convexity at the midpoint of a+2tv and a+2tw yields h(v+w)<=h(v)+h(w). Both sublinear difference inequalities imply Lipschitz continuity of h.

For a touching support of any finite continuous convex H, project (x,H(x)-1/n) to its closed epigraph. Existence follows by restricting distance minimization to a bounded closed ball. First variation along every feasible segment supplies a supporting unit normal at the nearest point. Its distance from (x,H(x)) tends to zero, and a subsequence of normals has a unit supporting limit at the graph point. The height coefficient is nonpositive because the epigraph is upward closed. It cannot be zero: a unit horizontal normal would bound its full spatial projection, which is the entire affine space. Consequently its vertical coefficient is strictly negative; division gives an affine support minorant. This NONZERO limiting vertical coefficient is essential.

Apply the construction to h at each v. If ell(x)+b<=h(x) touches at v, evaluating at tv for all t>=0 gives ell(v)<=h(v) from t to infinity, hence b>=0 by touching. At zero b<=0, so b=0 and ell(v)=h(v). The forms ell<=h are exactly K={ell:F(a+x)>=F(a)+ell(x) for every x}: one direction takes derivatives of the global inequality; the other uses h(x)<=F(a+x)-F(a). Thus K is nonempty closed convex, bounded by the norm bound on h applied to both signs, and compact. Moreover h(v)=max_{ell in K}ell(v) for every v. This proves the exact compact support representation, not merely existence of one subgradient.

At a crossing translate v to zero. Let K_i be the compact branch subdifferentials and h_i their support functions. In W=product L_i^*, K=product K_i is compact convex. Let S be the image of the ambient restriction map E^* -> W. It is a closed finite-dimensional linear subspace, although it need not be all of W. Suppose K and S are disjoint. Choose k0 in K minimizing squared distance to S, and q=projection_{S-perp}(k0), nonzero. For k in K, first variation toward k gives <q,k-k0>>=0, hence <q,k>>=||q||^2. Set z=-q. It annihilates S and max_K <z,k><= -||q||^2<0. Using the dual identification with vectors w_i in L_i, annihilation is the ACTUAL ambient equality sum_i w_i=0, and the strict bound is sum_i h_i(w_i)<0. The signs of this alternative are therefore correct.

The branch embeddings are rational, so the exact kernel of the ambient sum map has a rational basis. Approximate the separating tuple INSIDE that kernel by rational tuples. Continuity of h_i preserves strict negative cost. Drop zero entries. A common sufficiently small rational t>0 makes every endpoint v+t w_i lie in a genuine inherited cell incident to v; finiteness excludes all nonincident cells near v. For this fixed finite tuple, the derivative expansion gives sum_i(f_i(v+t w_i)-f(v))=t sum_i h_i(w_i)+o(t)<0. Equal weights 1/m give exactly barycenter v. The crossing is a rational vertex of the carrier, so these are legal finite printed endpoints. This contradicts PC. Thus K intersects S and an actual ambient preimage gives p_v supporting ALL incident complete branches. No direct-sum grouping of dependent branch barycenters occurs.

For sufficiency, a positive-dimensional convex cell contained in the finite union of affine branches is contained in one branch. If no branch contains its affine hull, choose a nonzero defining affine equation for each proper branch intersection with that hull. Their product is a nonzero polynomial and cannot vanish on an open relative interior, contradicting coverage. Once a branch contains the hull, it contains the cell. Cells on different branches therefore meet only at empty sets or the actual singleton branch intersections. Whenever cells from two branches contain that singleton, the complex common-face axiom makes it a vertex. Such cells exist at every crossing because each complete branch is covered by its cells. This proves that crossings are vertices on every rational carrier; it is not an extra chosen geometry assumption.

For a PCC whose center is away from crossings, all incident endpoint cells are on the unique branch, so ordinary convexity proves Jensen even for real endpoints. At a crossing v, use f(x_j)>=f(v)+p_v(x_j-v) for each endpoint, on whichever incident branch carries its cell. Summing with the actual nonnegative weights cancels the ambient form by the barycenter equality. These arguments hold on every rational carrier/refinement and for real center and endpoints. They also show why no global ambient convex extension is needed. This proves both directions of the criterion in the stated continuous class. The proofs supply the unnumbered incidence, local-Lipschitz, derivative, separation, rational-kernel and geometry claims of the paper as well as its numbered results.

notes.summary: Scoped global regularization PASS: actual irrational recession allowed, rational-spatial real-height majorants touch all finite crossings and strictly decrease globally before envelope MA.
notes.detailedSummary: The actual finite gradient polytope and exact recession epigraph use rational spatial generators with real heights. Whole-boundary dual continuity supplies finite rational samples; a closed primal hull has exact conjugate and global error. Projected lower faces give a rational complex. Finite exact contacts retain common supports, rational cuts glue all branches, and 4dyadic shifts give strict decrease and C+5/2. R230 actual envelopes enter before S272 completion.
notes.text:
I reconstruct full-affine approximation using the actual reference, actual real heights and exact recession, and then glue at every crossing. Fix saturated rational affine coordinates on a complete branch. For convex finite PA gamma, every full-dimensional cell's affine gradient is a global support: secants toward any other point start within that cell. Its affine expression is a minorant attained on the cell. Density of full-cell interiors and continuity give gamma(x)=max_j(a_j.x+b_j) for the ACTUAL finite real gradients and intercepts. Put h(x)=max_j a_j.x and Delta=conv{a_j}. Then |gamma-h| is bounded by max|b_j| and |f-h|<=D when |f-gamma|<=C.

The rational cell recession cones cover the whole space. Along any direction v, infinitely many points t_n v with t_n tending to infinity lie in one of finitely many closed cells. Divide that cell's affine inequalities by t_n; the limit v satisfies its recession inequalities. On such a cone gamma's cell gradient evaluates to h(v), by evaluating along a ray from any cell point and taking the recession limit. Bounded difference gives the SAME recession h for f at any base point. Positive growth gives h(v)>0 for v nonzero. Compactness of the unit sphere supplies h(v)>=b||v|| with b>0. If Delta failed to contain the radius-b ball about zero, nearest-point separation of a point of that ball from Delta would contradict this support inequality. Delta is a compact polytope with possibly irrational vertices; no gradients are rounded.

No carrying cell has nonzero lineality, since its gradient would have to be strictly positive on both v and -v. Each rational recession cone has rational ray generators by n1. On that cone h is exactly the cell gradient, so any conic decomposition of x by its rational generators lifts with equality to (x,h(x)). Therefore epi h is generated by the finite collection (r,h(r)) with RATIONAL spatial r and ACTUAL REAL heights, plus (0,1). Conversely sublinearity puts every such combination in epi h. This exact recession epigraph need not be a rational lifted polyhedron.

For f^*(p)=sup_x(p.x-f(x)), the finite domain is exactly Delta: on Delta, -f(0)<=f^*(p)<=D since p.x<=h(x); outside Delta, nearest-point separation gives v with p.v>h(v), and x=t v makes the conjugate infinite. It is convex and lower semicontinuous as a supremum of affine continuous functions. I check continuity on the WHOLE CLOSED polytope, not only its relative interior. Any finite convex lower-semicontinuous g on a compact polytope is bounded above by M, its largest vertex value. At p choose r>0 below every inactive slack divided by the corresponding nonzero constraint norm, in its affine span. If q is nearby and feasible, z=p+r(q-p)/||q-p|| is feasible: active inequalities remain valid along this direction at every positive scale, and inactive constraints retain their slack at radius r. For t=||q-p||/r<1, q=(1-t)p+t z, so g(q)<=g(p)+t(M-g(p)). This proves limsup<=g(p); lower semicontinuity supplies liminf>=g(p). Lower-dimensional and singleton polytopes use their own affine span. Applying this to f^* proves the required boundary continuity. Compact POLYTOPES are crucial to this argument.

By continuity of f, rational spatial x suffice in its conjugate supremum. At each p in Delta choose a rational x with dual error less than eta/2. Whole-boundary continuity of f^* and continuity of p.x-f(x) keep the error below eta in a relative neighborhood. Compactness selects finitely many samples A0. Append ANY prescribed finite rational contact set B and, if needed, one rational point to keep A nonempty. Appended sample terms never exceed f^*. Hence g_A(p)=max_{x in A}(p.x-f(x)) satisfies f^*-eta<=g_A<=f^* on ALL Delta. Heights remain the actual real values f(x), not rational approximations.

Let E_A=conv{(x,f(x)):x in A}+epi h. The hull is compact and the cone closed; convergence of a sequence in their sum has a subsequence of first summands converging, so the sum is closed. Finite hull-plus-cone elimination makes it a finite REAL polyhedron. Its spatial projection is the whole space and it is upward closed. The secant inequality f(y+v)<=f(y)+h(v) follows by comparing the secant at t=1 with its limit at infinity; bounded difference from h and its finite max formula identify that limit. Convex combinations of sample lifts lie above f, and adding an epi h vector preserves that relation. Thus E_A is inside epi f. Every vertical fiber is nonempty and closed with a finite attained lower minimum, bounded below by f. Write E_A=epi F_A. This finite convex function is continuous by n2 and f<=F_A. The sample lifts give F_A(b)<=f(b), so equality holds at EVERY appended contact.

The exact conjugate of F_A is g_A on Delta and infinite outside. The supremum of (p,-1) over the compact hull is g_A, while its supremum over epi h is zero on Delta and infinity otherwise. A finite continuous convex H obeys biconjugacy directly from n2's touching supports: a touching affine support realizes equality at x in sup_p(p.x-H^*(p)), and the conjugate definition gives the opposite inequality. Applying this to f and F_A and the dual error yields f<=F_A<=f+eta on the ENTIRE unbounded space. This is a global majorant estimate, not compact-set approximation.

Rational spatial PA membership needs an additional face argument. A lower face of E_A exposed by (p,-1) is the sum of the selected sample-hull face and the zero-exposed recession-cone face. They are generated by subsets of the finite sample lifts and recession lifts; the vertical generator is excluded. Its projection is consequently a rational spatial hull plus rational cone. The height on that face is the unique affine graph p.x-F_A^*(p), so projection is an affine isomorphism. All graph points have such nonvertical supports. There are finitely many lower facets and faces; their projections cover space. For two projected graph faces, their intersection equals the projection of their upstairs intersection because there is just one graph height at each spatial point. Upstairs intersections are common faces, and the affine graph projections preserve faces. All subfaces of these rational projected polyhedra are rational, so these projections give an actual finite rational spatial complex. F_A has REAL affine coefficients on it. This establishes the genuine scalar extension without an irrational max wall.

Its recession cone is exactly epi h. Inclusion is immediate. Conversely for a recession vector, divide translates by their parameter; bounded sample-hull parts vanish and the closed cone contains the limit. Equivalently the global bounded error identifies F_A's exact recession. Every affine minorant of f remains a minorant of F_A because F_A>=f. Appending B loses neither that support retention nor the exact recession or error. Convexity proves PC with all real endpoints; finite saturated divisor positivity is checked independently in n4. Thus the single-branch theorem uses no slope rounding or change of actual gamma.

For the arrangement, the finite contact set on branch i is every meeting point V intersect Q_i. At eta_n=2^{-n}, choose F_{i,n} with f_i<=F_{i,n}<=f_i+eta_n and F_{i,n}(v)=f(v). All common ambient supports from n2 remain minorants. Cut each branch carrier by d rational coordinate hyperplanes x_j=v_j at EVERY crossing, then refine the inherited carrier if needed. These cuts make v a vertex. Within one branch cells already meet in common faces; across different branches they meet only at the isolated crossings, now vertices. The finite union of carriers therefore is a genuine rational complex. The branch functions glue continuously by their equal values. The retained common supports and criterion in n2 prove PC, with one global error 0<=F_n-f<=eta_n on all branches and ends, and unchanged branch recessions.

Set G_n=F_n+4 eta_n. The common support intercept at each crossing shifts by the same constant. Globally 4 eta_n<=G_n-f<=5 eta_n, and G_{n+1}-f<=5 eta_n/2<4 eta_n<=G_n-f. Thus the sequence is STRICTLY decreasing everywhere, converges uniformly on all X, and ||G_n-gamma||<=C+5/2 for n>=1. The shifted G_n need not touch f; exact contact was required for F_n to glue. Uniform limits of continuous PC functions are continuous and pass every fixed finite printed inequality, giving exactly the asserted continuous relative completion domain.

Now all hypotheses of R230 are established: finite rational embedded positive balanced geometry, continuous actual PC reference and u in C_b. Its unrestricted actual P_gamma(u), not a PA-obstacle ansatz, is continuous PC with relative bound ||u||. Apply the just-proved construction to that ACTUAL function. Only afterwards apply S272 to every endpoint tuple, including these envelopes. The raw mass is the same M as gamma; moment and weak/BL uniformity retain the fixed-C height stated in n1. If bounded continuous obstacles converge uniformly, R230 gives uniform envelope convergence and a common C. Their bounded continuous gaps converge uniformly; weak C_b convergence of MA and common mass pass the contact integrals to the limit. This proves stability, not vanishing of contact. No density of arbitrary obstacles is assumed.

notes.summary: Primitive raw chain PASS: full BBGS commutation/refinement/balance with every-dimensional covolume conversion; saturated determinant, repeated-zero and d! factors reconstructed.
notes.detailedSummary: Real/signed/zero primitive recursion is lift-independent and converts to the negative BBGS unit-normal product with a_sigma/a_tau at every dimension. The full paired-perpendicular double-sum exchange, all subdivision cases and linear annihilation prove commutation/balance. Local supports give positivity; bounded primitive edges give raw mass and IBP. Consecutive saturated kernel factors telescope without added normalization; examples are exact but finite checks are not continuum certificates.
notes.text:
I reconstruct the finite primitive raw chain and its source conventions. On a common finite carrier the saturated lattice of a k-cell is N_sigma=N intersect span(sigma-sigma). For a balanced real weight c, the tangent-corrected formula is D_f c(tau)=sum_{sigma>tau} c(sigma) f_sigma(n_sigma/tau) - f_tau(sum_{sigma>tau} c(sigma)n_sigma/tau), using primitive inward quotient lifts and the linear parts of the actual real affine factors. Balance puts the sum in the tangent of tau. Replacing a lift by n+t with t tangent changes the two terms equally because continuous affine restrictions agree tangentially. This works for real signed and zero weights; intermediate cycles need not be effective for the algebraic assertions.

Choose a Euclidean metric and write a_sigma for the covolume of its saturated tangent lattice, a_vertex=1. A facet lattice basis extended by a primitive quotient lift is a cell lattice basis, so perpendicular height is a_sigma/a_tau. Thus the perpendicular component of n_sigma/tau is (a_sigma/a_tau) nu_sigma/tau for inward unit conormal nu. Put C_sigma=a_sigma c_sigma. Lattice balance modulo the tangent is equivalent to the Euclidean conormal sum being zero. Embed x as (x,1) in E direct-sum R with product metric. The image lies in an affine hyperplane not through zero, is cellwise affine injective, and preserves all tangent lengths because tangent last coordinates are zero. This satisfies the ORIGINAL BBGS quasi-embedding requirement rather than treating an embedding through zero as that requirement.

Extend f_tau to one ambient affine linear part l. Subtracting l and tangential components in the raw formula leaves sum c_sigma(f_sigma-l)(perpendicular n). In BBGS, the product B uses NEGATIVE inward-unit slopes. Balance cancels l in B_{-f}(C), giving B_{-f}(a c)(tau)=a_tau D_f c(tau). The identity holds at EVERY recursive dimension, not merely the top, and ends with a_vertex=1. Affine constants disappear from slopes; the homogeneous extension on (x,1) has the same tangent evaluations. Saturation and primitive quotient units, not Euclidean unit lengths alone, determine the numerical raw coefficients.

Here is the full commuting exchange behind original BBGS3.15. For a codimension-two face rho of an actual k-cell sigma, quotient by its tangent. The resulting pointed two-dimensional wedge has exactly two boundary facets tau,tau'; nonsimplicial sigma does not add a third wedge boundary ray. Write v1=(1,0), v2=(cos(theta),sin(theta)), 0<theta<pi. The inward perpendiculars are (0,1) and (sin(theta),-cos(theta)). Solving gives nu_sigma/tau=a v_tau/rho+b v_tau'/rho and nu_sigma/tau'=a v_tau'/rho+b v_tau/rho with a=-cot(theta), b=csc(theta). Both use the paired inward orientation.

The two negative signs in B_f B_g cancel. Its rho coefficient is
sum_{tau>rho} sum_{sigma>tau} C_sigma g_sigma(nu_sigma/tau) f_tau(v_tau/rho).
Group by sigma>rho and expand the paired perpendiculars. The result is
sum_{sigma>rho} C_sigma [ a_{sigma,rho} sum_{sigma>tau>rho} f_tau(v_tau/rho) g_tau(v_tau/rho)

 + b sum_tau f_tau'(v_tau'/rho) g_tau(v_tau/rho) ]

notes.text:
At ANY crossing v and for ANY admitted actual real reference, I reconstruct the finite PA negative-contact witness. Choose one incident complete branch with tangent L1 and positive weight c1, and a rational nonzero line T in another. Pairwise isolated intersection gives L1 intersect T=0. Prescribe a saturated dual basis of L1 and zero on T, then extend a rational basis of L1 direct-sum T to the ambient space. This gives rational ambient forms ell_1,...,ell_d; the direct-sum assertion concerns ONLY those two spaces, not the dependent collection of all branches. The homogeneous ambient convex rational PA h=sum_j|ell_j| is PC on the actual tangent star and flat on both directions of T. It has a finite rational hyperplane fan and a genuine rational two-endpoint flat PCC.

The tangent top cycle is the sum of the incident complete planes; nonincident branches have positive distance from v. Its positive complete subcycle c1[L1] has an effective balanced residual by n1. On each incident branch use saturated coordinates to form the restriction matrix A_i. By n4 and additivity in the cycle its raw top atom is m0=2^d d! sum_i c_i |det A_i| >=2^d d! c1>0, since A_1 is the identity. The other chosen branch has the kernel direction T, hence zero determinant, while furnishing the flat relation. Additional branches have nonnegative contributions and cannot cancel the positive atom. This handles actual REAL weights, not merely rational examples.

The coefficient-cone and actual-reference realization need their own proof. On a fixed finite rational carrier continuous affine coefficient lists satisfy rational linear shared-face equations. At a face take rational generators for all incident feasible directions, including both signs of tangent lineality, as columns of U. If s is the list of corresponding slopes, existence of one ambient supporting form is exactly s in R_+^m+image(U^T). This cone is finitely generated (use both signs of an image basis), hence closed by n1. If s lies outside it, let y be its nearest point and z=y-s. First variation, scaling along the cone and testing its lineality give z in the dual cone, z>=0, U z=0, and z.s=-||z||^2<0. Thus the nonnegative kernel relation has strictly negative cost. Conversely all such costs nonnegative imply membership and support. The signs and closedness are explicit.

There are finitely many rational generators for {lambda>=0:U lambda=0}. One constructive proof reduces supports: if a positive supported kernel has dimension greater than one, subtract a multiple of lambda from an independent kernel vector to make a mixed-sign vector; move both ways until a positive coordinate disappears and express lambda between the two smaller-support relations. Repeat. A terminal one-dimensional supported kernel has a rational generator by Gaussian elimination. These finitely many relation costs are rational linear inequalities in the affine coefficients. A negative relation at a rational relative-face center can be realized with one small rational endpoint scale in the incident cells, contradicting printed PC. At real centers, slopes are constant on the face and both tangent signs are tested, so the same support conditions apply. In the present complete-branch arrangement local supports imply local branch convexity, which propagates to whole branch convexity by the strict maximum argument in n2. A local common support at a crossing then supports each whole convex branch by secants. Thus n2 implies all PCCs. No unsupported automatic local-to-global claim is needed for the collar functions.

Let actual gamma lie in the minimal face of this rational coefficient cone. Its active equalities cut out a rational subspace W. Every inactive finite PC inequality and every nonzero generator recession-growth inequality is strictly positive at gamma. In rational coordinates on W, choose small rational r>0 and rational b close to gamma so the simplex with vertices b-r sum e_j and b+r e_j is in that strict neighborhood and encloses gamma in its relative interior. Its actual barycentric coefficients t_i are POSITIVE REAL numbers summing to ONE. The coefficient identity gamma=sum_i t_i gamma_i is exact; each rational-affine gamma_i is continuous PC with positive growth on the same rational carrier. A zero-dimensional face is immediate. This is a decomposition of the finite reference coefficients, not rational approximation of arbitrary endpoints. It preserves the active equalities exactly and uses no tolerance to decide them.

Choose a common rational polyhedral norm rho, a rational alpha>0 slower than all gamma_i recessions and rational C0>max_i gamma_i(v). On each branch, finite vertices plus rational recession generators give gamma_i(x)>=a_i rho(x-v)-b_i for some a_i>alpha and finite b_i; one can also obtain this from its actual finite max recession formula. Thus Psi_i=max(gamma_i,C0+alpha rho(x-v)) is rational PA PC, equals the norm entry near v and gamma_i outside a compact set. Ambient norm restriction is PC. Choose a common rational star radius r small enough for the actual tangent fan, L with |h|<=L rho there, and rational delta,t>0 with delta L<=alpha/2 and t<alpha r/4. Inside rho<r set G_i=max(Psi_i,C0+t+delta h), leaving Psi_i outside. On r/2<=rho<r, the norm entry exceeds the jet by at least alpha rho/2-t>0. Hence an unchanged collar joins the two definitions, while near v the raised jet dominates and EVERY G_i has the identical germ C0+t+delta h.

On the inner star, each active entry has an ambient local support; a support for any active maximum entry remains a support for the maximum at ties. The unchanged collar supplies supports across the boundary. By the preceding complete-branch propagation, each G_i is globally PC on every carrier. All max comparisons and cuts use rational-affine coefficients, so each G_i has a finite rational carrier. Take a common refinement and put F=sum_i t_i G_i. Its coefficients are REAL but its carrier is rational; positive sums preserve every PC inequality. F-gamma=sum_i t_i(G_i-gamma_i) is bounded. Because sum_i t_i=1, its germ is exactly C0+t+delta h, with raw atom delta^d m0>0. This common-jet construction uses the positive CONVEX decomposition, not gamma=gamma'+epsilon gamma0 from the moment proof. Adding an unrelated residual gamma germ would destroy flatness; taking a max against irrational actual gamma could create an irrational spatial wall. Neither operation occurs.

For the envelope choose rational R>0 small enough that the closed rho ball has this exact germ, meets only affine cells incident to v in a common rational carrier of F,gamma,[X], and contains no other vertex of that carrier. Such a radius exists because there are finitely many closed nonincident cells and other vertices. On incident affine cells every inactive inequality at v retains positive slack in the ball, so radial extension to its boundary stays in that same cell whenever its ray direction satisfies the active inequalities. Set B_R=(R-rho(x-v))_+ and u=F-gamma+B_R. This is bounded continuous REAL PA on rational geometry. F is an actual unrestricted relative competitor below F+B_R, since F-gamma is bounded.

Consider ANY raw printed-PC competitor q below F+B_R, with its actual growth upper bound. Opposite rational boundary points of T, normalized by the rational norm, have barycenter v and equal F value F(v), because the jet is flat there. Their incident cells make the two-endpoint relation legal. Thus q(v)<=F(v). For rational x inside the ball, y=v+R(x-v)/rho(x-v) is a rational boundary point in the same incident affine cell. The chord between rational endpoints v and y, centered at x, is legal because its center face is contained in that cell. Since F is affine along the radial segment and q(y)<=F(y), it yields q(x)<=F(x). Outside the ball q<=F directly from the obstacle.

For any real x use shrinking rational simplices in its ACTUAL relative rational face that contain x. Rational affine coordinates allow such simplices with vertices arbitrarily close to x and inside the relative face by inactive slack. All endpoints are rational and their assigned cell contains the center face, so the printed inequality applies with real barycentric coefficients. The already established rational bounds q(x_j)<=F(x_j), plus continuity of F, give q(x)<=F(x). NO continuity or semicontinuity of q is assumed. This covers real boundary points as well. Consequently every unrestricted competitor is bounded by F, and the exact ACTUAL envelope P_gamma(u)=F is established BEFORE measuring it.

F is already an actual finite PA-PC relative function, so a constant approximation sequence supplies the completed-domain antecedent. Refinement independence from n4 gives zero artificial atoms on the roof cuts: adding the obstacle carrier does not add divisor coefficients of F. The only original carrier vertex inside the roof support is v. The gap F-gamma-u=-B_R equals -R at v and vanishes outside; possible boundary atoms have zero gap. The contact integral is therefore exactly -R delta^d m0<0. This is a genuine finite-PA witness for every crossing and actual reference. Universal continuous-PC regularization does not imply contact.
